ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a line graph changing with years; the horizontal axis is 1950, 1960, 1970, 1980, 1990, 2000, and 2010, and the vertical labels include “urban population (hundred million)” and “urbanization level (%).” There are four curves in the figure, labeled ①, ②, ③, and ④ respectively: ① is located at a relatively high position, with values rising from more than 50 to more than 70; ② is also at a percentage-scale level, roughly rising from more than ten to more than 40; ③ is at a lower position but rises relatively quickly; ④ is the lowest and grows relatively slowly. Then reason: According to the value ranges in the figure, ① and ② more conform to percentage curves of urbanization level; ③ and ④ have lower values, more conforming to curves of urban population size. Developing countries have a large population base and fast growth of urban population, so the urban population should be the higher and faster-rising ③; developed countries have relatively smaller urban population size and slower growth, so it should correspond to ④. Therefore, the curve representing the urban population of developed countries in the figure is the 4th curve.
